messages:
IncidentBot: [PAGER] GPU pool 'inference-us-west-gpu' at 100% capacity; HPA external metrics missing for 4m. Autoscaler not increasing replicas. Paging @oncall.
Alice Chen: Oncall Alice here. Who's looking at HPA/metrics? Quick surface-level notes: customers seeing 5xx, dispatcher queue rising.
Devon Park: I'm on it. Cluster = prod-us-west-2, node pool gpu-pool currently 6/6. HPA "inference-worker-hpa" is stuck because external metric 'gpu/queue_len_ext' returns no data.
Samira Khan: I see a big spike from an ad-hoc analytics batch around 19:46 UTC. Dispatcher queue went from ~80 -> 900 in 10m. Autoscaler should have reacted.
Alice Chen: Can someone check metrics-adapter and Prometheus scrapes?
Devon Park: Running: kubectl -n infra logs deploy/metrics-adapter --tail=100
Devon Park (logs): "WARN: Prometheus query timeout for query 'sum(queue_len{cluster=\"prod-us-west-2\"})'" "ERROR: external metrics handler: upstream error: 504 Gateway Timeout" "killed process due to OOM"
Samira Khan: Prometheus itself is overloaded; target scrape failure rate high. One Prometheus replica restarted due to OOM earlier.
InfraBot: Alert: Prometheus replica set 'prom-prod' restarted at 19:54:12 UTC due to node memory pressure.
Alice Chen: Immediate plan: 1) reduce customer impact by adding capacity manually 2) restart metrics-adapter and Prom replica(s) 3) provide customer update. Assign: Devon = adapter/prom, Samira = manual scale & dispatcher tuning, Alice = comms and lead.
Samira Khan: Manually scaling node pool: gcloud container clusters resize prod-us-west-2 --node-pool=gpu-pool --num-nodes=10
Samira Khan (cmd): "Resizing... done. New size: 10 nodes."
Devon Park: Restarting metrics-adapter and scaling Prometheus: kubectl -n infra rollout restart deployment/metrics-adapter; kubectl -n monitoring scale statefulset/prom-prod --replicas=3
Devon Park (logs post-restart): "INFO: metrics-adapter listening" "INFO: connected to prometheus-prod:9090"
Alice Chen: HPA still shows no metrics. Devon can you curl the adapter endpoint for the external metric?
Devon Park: curl -s 'http://metrics-adapter.infra.svc.cluster.local/apis/external.metrics.k8s.io/v1beta1/namespaces/inference/gpu/queue_len_ext' | jq
Devon Park (output): "error: no metrics available"
Devon Park: Prometheus query works in UI: sum(queue_len{cluster=\"prod-us-west-2\"}) = 820. Adapter returning nothing intermittently 3 probably due to adapter timeouts when Prom responds slowly.
Samira Khan: Dispatcher tuning: increased dispatcher replicas and raised concurrency limits to drain queue quickly. kubectl -n inference scale deployment/dispatcher --replicas=8
Samira Khan (metrics): queue length dropping from 920 -> 320 in 7m as new pods come up.
Alice Chen: Customer impact assessment: Samira, what percent of requests failing and which customers most impacted?
Samira Khan: APILog shows 5xx rate for generation endpoints up by 14% in US-WEST. Top impacted customers: alpha-ops (30% of their calls failed), beta-app (15%), small tenants aggregated ~8%. Posting status page now.
Alice Chen: Devon, any chance to create a temporary synthetic metric to force HPA to scale while we restore the full pipeline?
Devon Park: Yes. I'll push a synthetic external metric via the adapter's supported push endpoint and map it in external metrics config. Applying a lightweight exporter to /metrics-ext.
Devon Park (cmd): kubectl -n infra apply -f /tmp/synthetic-metric-adapter.yaml
Devon Park: Synthetic metric visible to adapter; HPA now reads value and desiredReplicas jumps. HPA Desired: 18, Current: 6.
InfraBot: Deployment: inference-worker upscaling initiated due to HPA desired change.
Samira Khan: New worker pods are provisioning; queue now trending down to ~80.
Alice Chen: Customer update posted: "We are adding capacity and working on restoring metric pipelines. Expected improved stability within 30-45 minutes."
Devon Park: Post-restart Prometheus scrape success improved after we cordoned the noisy node and increased memory for Prometheus pods. Adapter started returning metrics normally.
Devon Park (curl): [{"metricName":"gpu/queue_len_ext","value":"72","timestamp":"2026-03-15T21:05:12Z"}]
Alice Chen: HPA events show successful scaling to new replica count. Any errors or regressions?
Samira Khan: No regressions observed. Latency and error rates are dropping. Queue at 24 and steady.
Alice Chen: Root cause hypotheses: primary = Prometheus replica OOM/flapping causing scrape gaps -> metrics-adapter timeouts -> HPA sees no external metrics -> autoscaler didn't scale -> queue grew. Contributing = sudden batch load from analytics.
Devon Park: Short-term remediation we applied: scaled GPU pool, restarted metrics-adapter, added synthetic metric fallback, cordoned noisy node, increased Prom resources.
Alice Chen: Post-incident action items: 1) Postmortem (owner Devon) 2) Add alert for external metrics missing >30s (owner infra) 3) Add synthetic heartbeat metric permanently for external metrics pipeline (owner infra) 4) Add Prometheus resource sizing/runbook for memory pressure (owner monitoring) 5) Limit big batch jobs or require schedule (owner analytics lead).
Samira Khan: I'll keep monitoring for 30m before closing. I'll also follow up with analytics team about job scheduling.
Alice Chen: Handoff: I'm going offline in 25m. Devon take ownership for postmortem and follow-ups. Summary: scaled manually, restored adapter/prom metrics, synthetic metric unblocked HPA, queue drained, customers recovering. Contact Devon @devon if needed.
Devon Park: Acknowledged handoff. I'll produce the postmortem and coordinate follow-ups.
IncidentBot: Incident state: mitigated -> monitoring. Duration: ~00:43. Incident lead: Alice Chen. Assigned follow-ups: devon@redwood (postmortem), samira@redwood (customer comms), infra@redwood (alerts/runbook).
